blurb: What a Claude Code task really costs, and how far each plan carries you — every coefficient measured from real session transcripts instead of assumed.

name: time study
blurb: Where the hours actually went on an AI-assisted project. Every hour is attributed from session records and git history, and the counterfactual is shown as two adjustable models rather than asserted as a number.

name: roadkeep
blurb: Owns the writes to your ROADMAP, CHANGELOG and IMPROVEMENTS, so the format is a schema at the point of insertion instead of a convention you have to remember.

name: commitclerk
blurb: Better git commit messages in one command. It reads your staged diff, asks an LLM for a Conventional Commits message, shows it to you, and commits.

name: Claude Code Tray
blurb: Your Claude Code usage, always in the tray. A native Windows monitor that shows your rate-limit percentage as a crisp, DPI-aware icon.

name: FreeWilly
blurb: Docker on Windows without Docker Desktop: upstream Moby in a WSL2 distro it owns, the docker_engine pipe your tools already look for, and one window of containers.

name: winwright
blurb: Drive a Windows desktop app from a test and report what was actually observed. Four verdicts rather than two, so a check that never ran is never reported as one that passed.
